user_request: Preserve the engineering-completion estimate table from this conversation and regenerate it with delta improvement when the user returns after several hours.
percentage_definition: Rough judgment about implementation, targeted tests and integration already accomplished, not formal acceptance, time remaining, executable-byte ownership or a weighted whole-OS score.
scope: Existing M00-M13 McKernel roadmap. The supported configuration includes the separate Linux control kernel; these estimates do not establish independent operation without Linux.

provenance.source: Exact ranges presented in chat and accepted by the user as the comparison baseline.

comparison_policy: Preserve this baseline unchanged; record later comparisons in new records.
When the user returns, show M00-M13 with baseline estimate, current estimate, delta in percentage points and concrete newly implemented/tested/integrated behavior with source/evidence references.
Keep current estimates and deltas explicitly subjective and low confidence. This is not a formal acceptance score.
For a single numerical delta, explicitly use the change between the baseline and current range midpoints; label it estimated percentage points, not measured improvement.
Do not infer a percentage increase from elapsed time, tokens, agent activity, commits, code volume or unchanged historical evidence.
If the engineering evidence does not justify revising the estimate, retain it and separately describe useful prerequisite work or unresolved measurement.
Allow unchanged or negative deltas when integration failures or newly discovered defects warrant them. Do not promise that every row will improve.
Milestones overlap, share dependencies and differ in size; never average or sum the row percentages into a whole-OS completion claim.
Formal gate/case/language acceptance remains governed by the original contracts and is reported separately.
Continue the existing image-first autonomous campaign; capturing this baseline is not a checkpoint stop, restart, workload release or goal-completion instruction.
